segment_text: 2.8 Transfer of Miltenyi Products. Bellicum shall have the right to transfer Miltenyi Product(s) purchased hereunder, or to request from Miltenyi, by notice in writing, that Miltenyi Deliver any Miltenyi Product(s) purchased hereunder to an Affiliate of Bellicum or a Subcontractor or Licensee of Bellicum Product designated by Bellicum, solely for the purpose of the Permitted Use, subject to the payment to Miltenyi of all additional expenses (if any) incurred by Miltenyi in connection with such provision and transfer of Miltenyi Product(s) to Bellicum's designee; and provided that in each case: (i) each Subcontractor or Licensee of Bellicum to whom Miltenyi Products are transferred shall be bound in writing by limitations and obligations that are consistent with the corresponding limitations and obligations imposed on Bellicum 8 Miltenyi Biotec-Bellicum Supply Agreement (Execution Copy, March 27, 2019) hereunder and under the Quality Agreement, as applicable; and (ii) notwithstanding the transfer of any Miltenyi Product purchased hereunder, Bellicum will nevertheless continue to remain fully and primarily responsible and liable to Miltenyi for payment of the Product Price and for the use of the Miltenyi Product by any Subcontractor and Licensee to whom a Miltenyi Product is transferred.

annotator_notes:
The main right of C04-033, the segment's FIRST item. Batch 5, seed 20260919 hard queue, position 15 -- THE LAST HARD-QUEUE ENTRY.

SEGMENT SHAPE. C04-033, 1,306 chars. BOTH GUARDS RUN BEFORE ANY ANNOTATION. F27 (splitter over-split): CLEAN -- zero redaction-induced splits, zero abbreviations, so the splitter's 2 fragments are both real (a heading and one long sentence). Section 8.7 (page furniture): the 74-char running header IS present, at [840:914], with page-number prefix 8 -- exactly as the 43-page measurement on C04-144 predicted.

THREE SPANS, ONE SENTENCE. main right [35:971] (item C04-12); sub-clause (i) [601:971] NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING, inside the main span; sub-clause (ii) split at [982:1189] (item C04-13, the PAY half) and [1190:1306] (the ABSORB half, dispositioned out). The two ITEM spans are DISJOINT -- the gap is '; and (ii) ' -- so unlike E03-04/E03-05's nested pair section 4.1 cannot collide, and (ii) needed no section 8.3.1 shared-subject treatment because it carries its own subject and modal ('Bellicum will nevertheless continue to remain').

A CITATION OF MINE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN DROPPED. Drafting this segment I cited C04-05 as the precedent for mapping an agentless 'shall be bound' to ENSURE and for promoting Bellicum into the obligor slot. READING ITS COMMITTED SPAN FALSIFIES BOTH USES: C04-05 is "Bellicum shall use, and WILL CAUSE its Subcontractors and Licensees to use, Miltenyi Products in accordance with all Applicable Laws..." -- an ACTIVE construction with an explicit CAUSATIVE and obligor Bellicum as the STATED agent. It establishes ENSURE for "will cause X to do Y", a named-agent causative; it says nothing about an agentless 'X shall be bound'. The reviewer's standing instruction to verify a precedent's span before citing it is what caught this.

AND THE PROMOTION I PROPOSED CONTRADICTED MY OWN REASONING FROM FOUR SEGMENTS EARLIER. I argued obligor ABSENT for C10-03's agentless passive on section 3.5.3's grounds, then proposed promoting Bellicum here from a possessive ('of Bellicum') and a comparison phrase ('imposed on Bellicum') -- the exact inference section 3.5.3's own C04-087 case forbids ("a possessive on a place is not a duty-bearer; reading one as the obligor is section 3.5's forbidden inference"). Recorded because the inconsistency is the useful part: the rule was applied correctly when the span had no plausible candidate and incorrectly when a party name happened to be nearby.

MODALITY MAY. "shall have the right to" -- C13-03's construction, section 3.2's table.

THE MAIN RIGHT IS DISJUNCTIVE AND IS F28's SECOND INSTANCE -- WITH A STATE F28's FORCING FUNCTION DID NOT ANTICIPATE: THERE IS NO PRIMACY SIGNAL AT ALL. "Bellicum shall have the right to TRANSFER Miltenyi Product(s) purchased hereunder, OR to REQUEST from Miltenyi, by notice in writing, that Miltenyi Deliver any Miltenyi Product(s) ... to an Affiliate of Bellicum or a Subcontractor or Licensee". One right, two alternative performances, the obligor choosing.

  F28 was opened at C04-10, where the limb choice was settled by the contract's own qualifying language ("promptly and diligently" attaching to the negotiate limb and nothing to the modify limb). ITS FORCING FUNCTION ASKS FOR "a second instance, most informatively one where the TEXTUALLY PRIMARY limb is the OFF-TAXONOMY one", to test whether the primacy principle holds independently of taxonomy convenience. THIS INSTANCE ANSWERS A DIFFERENT QUESTION INSTEAD: neither limb carries a performance adverb or any other primacy marker, so there is NO SIGNAL TO READ. Verified by execution rather than by eye -- a scan for performance adverbs over the main right returns none attached to either limb. NO SIGNAL WAS INVENTED; the absence is reported as the finding.

  THE PRINCIPLE PROPOSED AND REVIEWER-RULED: ANNOTATE THE LIMB WHOSE PERFORMANCE IS THE OBLIGOR'S OWN. Limb 1 is Bellicum transferring -- obligor and performance aligned. Limb 2's substantive performance is MILTENYI's ("that Miltenyi Deliver"); Bellicum's own act there is only REQUESTING, so annotating limb 2 would put a requester in the obligor slot against another party's performance, which a single obligor/action pair represents poorly and which would mis-describe who must do what. That is a STRUCTURAL ground about the IR's own fields, not a reading of the text's emphasis, which is why it survives the absence of a primacy signal.

  STATED AGAINST INTEREST, THE SAME DISCLOSURE C04-10 CARRIES: the principle HAPPENS to select the limb whose verb is a taxonomy member (TRANSFER is in ACTIONS; 'request' is in section 8.8's own named genuine-gap list). THAT ALIGNMENT IS COINCIDENTAL AND IS NOT THE REASONING. Had limb 2 been the obligor's-own-performance limb, this principle would have selected it and the item would have carried action_not_in_taxonomy.

  THE DISJUNCTION ITSELF REMAINS UNTAGGED, per F28: ast.Obligation has one action field and no alternation, so annotating either limb asserts a right the contract does not confine itself to. Direction OVERSTATING. No tag is minted -- F28 now has its second instance and its forcing function is PARTIALLY met (a second instance, but not the off-taxonomy-primary case it asked for), which is recorded in F28's row rather than here.

ACTION TRANSFER, a literal taxonomy member. ACCEPT-SET IS A SINGLETON ON A PRINCIPLED GROUND RATHER THAN FOR WANT OF CANDIDATES: DELIVER and PROVIDE are arguably defensible for "transfer products", but DELIVER IS LIMB 2's OWN VERB ("that Miltenyi Deliver"), so admitting it would make clause 2 unable to distinguish which limb an extraction found -- the accept-set would score a correct read of the WRONG limb as correct. No section 8.8 tag is owed; TRANSFER is the verb the sentence uses.

OBLIGEE ABSENT. The transfer runs to "an Affiliate of Bellicum or a Subcontractor or Licensee of Bellicum Product designated by Bellicum" -- all unnamed third parties section 21 R3 excludes from any registry, and none is the contract counterparty. Miltenyi IS named in-span, but as the payee of incidental expenses (inside condition 2) and as the addressee of limb 2's request -- NOT as the recipient of the transfer this item annotates. Section 3.5's positional test therefore finds no party occupying the recipient slot; section 3.5.4 is cited because obligee assignment does not turn on modality.

UNDERSPECIFIED TRUE on section 3.9 trigger 1, once: obligee is ABSENT. Obligor "Bellicum" resolves in evals/registry/C04.json (verified by reading it). temporal: null is never a trigger.

OBJECT_CLASS 'product'. Head noun of the object phrase ("Miltenyi Product(s) purchased hereunder") is "product", which is both the slot and the head-only member section 3.6's v0.58 forward rule requires. 'miltenyi_product' was DELIBERATELY NOT AUTHORED: it encodes a contracting party's name, which is the hazard section 3.6.1 exists to prevent even though Miltenyi is not THIS item's obligor or obligee. SECTION 3.6.2 CLEAR: "product" is not the nominal of TRANSFER ("transfer" is), so clauses 2 and 5 stay independent.

TEMPORAL NULL -- cell (c) in the three-way C04-11 established: the clause contains NO timing on the right at all. Not a REACHABILITY gap and not an unrepresentable form. Section 3.7's condition for null is met exactly.

CONDITIONS -- THREE ENTRIES by section 17.1's marker count, and ONE CANDIDATE MARKER WAS A FALSE POSITIVE CAUGHT BY READING THE FLAGGED CONTEXT. A scan found four hits; "(if any)" at main-relative [411] is a PARENTHETICAL HEDGE on whether expenses exist, sitting INSIDE condition 2, not a scoping marker. Section 17.1 says count scoping markers, not word occurrences; this is Standing Principle 7's shape and was caught by reading the context rather than the count.
  ENTRY 1 "solely for the purpose of the Permitted Use" -- THE SET'S FIRST PURPOSE-ADJUNCT CONDITION, and it is NOT in section 3.8.2's marker set. REVIEWER-RULED a condition ON THE REMOVAL TEST ALONE: delete it and the right covers transfers for ANY purpose, which widens WHEN THE RIGHT APPLIES rather than which products it covers -- the object is Miltenyi Products either way. THE COUNTER-READING IS RECORDED AS FORWARD GUIDANCE: it can be read as object scope under section 3.8.2's F8 test (E05-P1's "in connection with any action, suit or other proceeding" shape), because "which transfers are permitted" is arguably a set-of-things question. Rejected because the set that widens is the set of CIRCUMSTANCES, not of objects. No queue row; a second purpose-adjunct instance should be decided by citing this one.
  ENTRY 2 "subject to the payment to Miltenyi of all additional expenses (if any) incurred by Miltenyi in connection with such provision and transfer of Miltenyi Product(s) to Bellicum's designee" -- C10-01's locked "Subject to the Distributor fulfilling all the conditions in this clause 10" is the precedent. Removal test: delete and the right is exercisable without paying Miltenyi's costs.
  ENTRY 3 "provided that in each case: (i) each Subcontractor or Licensee ... as applicable" -- SECTION 3.8.1 BRANCH 2. Branch 1 FAILS because (i) was ruled STATUS rather than a duty (see the segment file), so it cannot be a separate obligation; branch 2 then makes it a verbatim condition on this right. RULE A APPLIES: what precedes it is "; and ", so the quote begins at "provided that", not "and provided that" -- C04-01's clause-7 failure avoided by rule.
  CONVENTION EXPOSURE, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO A SCORING RUN. Section 3.8.2 says in terms that Rules A and B are unvalidated against model behaviour and "neither may be assumed to fix anything". The adverse precedent is C11-094, whose two-entry gold was emitted as ONE comma-joined string on 2 of 3 runs at temperature 0. Three entries is GOLD's convention here, not a prediction. Unlike C04-11, THIS ITEM IS NOT EXCLUDED FROM SECTION 9.1's IN-FORCE DENOMINATOR BY A REPRESENTATIONAL TAG -- corpus_artifact_in_span is CORPUS_DEFECT, which section 9.1 ADMITS -- so a clause-7 convention miss here would land on the IN-FORCE figure, not only on all-items. That is a materially worse exposure than C04-11's and is disclosed as such.

CORPUS_ARTIFACT_IN_SPAN (section 8.7). The header splice at [840:914] falls INSIDE this item's span [35:971] -- verified arithmetically, not assumed -- so the tag attaches here rather than being a disposition-only note.
